summary.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready” and is the standardized simplified counterpart of 備. A proposed analysis of 備 shows a person carrying an arrow container, linking the scene with preparedness; another analysis reads the graph as a picture of a quiver. These are interpretations of 備’s construction, not proof of the word’s earliest spoken meaning.

formation.text: The proposed main analysis of 備 combines 人, a person, with 𤰈, interpreted as an arrow container or quiver; the person carrying it suggests preparedness. Shuowen and another analysis assign 𤰈 a phonetic role, though its historical sound relation to 備 is not independently established here. A competing analysis treats 備 as a whole-graph picture of a quiver. 备 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 備.

components.text: Within 備, 人 represents the person in the proposed carrying scene. This breakdown is disputed because another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.
Within 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container, or a quiver. It also has a proposed phonetic role, but the depicted object’s original name and pronunciation are not independently recovered.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin readings of 𤰈 and 備 are both bèi, but that match does not establish their historical sound relation. The pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are not recovered.

sound.text: Both 𤰈 and 備 are listed with the modern Mandarin reading bèi. This current match does not establish that 𤰈 supplied 備’s historical sound.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but its earliest appearance and the sequence among these categories are unresolved.

The modern printed right-hand form 𤰇 is described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. Some bronze forms also change 𤰈’s lower part to 用, tentatively treated as a sound element; these reports do not establish a dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme standardized 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 is documented as a variant of 備, but the evidence does not establish that 备 was specifically derived from 俻.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation may explain the graph’s association with readiness, but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. 備 is also reported as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” in a bronze inscription. This is reported as a whole-graph loan; the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are unrecovered, so the sound match cannot be verified.

Reported meanings include prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these senses.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver interpretation may help explain preparedness, but does not prove this was the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss includes “cautious” or “careful”; this does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.
A bronze inscription reportedly reuses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver.” The proposed sound-based borrowing does not verify that 箙 sounded like the pictured container’s unrecovered original name.
